cards.explanation: The dispute is over which of them should be considered the greatest. Luke says a dispute arose among the disciples as to exactly that. Picture a group chat that went sideways, except everybody is sitting at the same table. I think that table got quiet in a hurry.

The answer is True. Jesus tells them, “But you shall not be like them.” The kings of the Gentiles, the nations outside Israel, lord it over people, and the disciples are not to follow that example. Jesus gives them a different way to live, friends, and He's about to say what it looks like.

The answer is serves, friends. Jesus says, “…and the one who leads like the one who serves.” That's the opposite of what the kings of the Gentiles do. Leading by serving is like the head of a bakery who stays late to scrub the pans. I know a stamper who would look pretty good doing it.

The answer is False. Jesus asks who is greater, the one who reclines or the one who serves, and agrees it's the one who reclines. Then He turns it around: “But I am among you as one who serves.” The One at the table is the One serving. That sure beats any of us fighting over a seat.

The answer is His Father, friends. Jesus says, “And I bestow on you a kingdom, just as My Father has bestowed one on Me…” The kingdom He gives them comes the same way His own did. Think of Him passing down a recipe He was given Himself.
The answer is table, bakers. Jesus says, “…so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom…” I spent years in a junk drawer, so a seat at a table sounds like a promotion to me.

The answer is judging the twelve tribes of Israel. Jesus says they will “…sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” He says it in the same talk where He answers their dispute over who's greatest. I think that's one humbling seat at the table.

The answer is that Jesus prayed that Simon's faith will not fail. Jesus says to Simon, “But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail.” Simon is the disciple Jesus also named Peter (Luke 6:14). Satan, the devil, has asked to sift them like wheat, and Jesus has prayed for him. That's Jesus covering Simon.

The answer is even to prison and to death, friends. Peter, the disciple also called Simon (Luke 6:14), says, “Lord, I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.” That's a big promise to make at a table. Next Jesus answers him.

The answer is that Peter will deny three times that he knows Jesus. Jesus says, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.” It's hard to hear right after Peter's big promise. I think that one stings.

The answer is Nothing, bakers. Jesus asks, “When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?” and they answer, “Nothing.” Without a purse, bag or sandals, they still lacked nothing. That's a one-word answer you don't see every day.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “Now, however, the one with a purse should take it, and likewise a bag…” That's a change from the time He sent them out with no purse or bag. Things are different now, and He tells them so plainly.
The answer is buy, friends. Jesus says, “and the one without a sword should sell his cloak and buy one.” He tells them to sell the cloak to get it. That's a big trade, and I'd be asking questions.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “For I tell you that this Scripture must be fulfilled in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the transgressors.’ For what is written about Me is reaching its fulfillment.” The words He points to come from the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 53:12). He says the writing about Him is reaching its fulfillment.
The answer is False. When the disciples say, “Look, Lord, here are two swords,” Jesus answers, “That is enough…” He doesn't send them off for more. The story still has more to tell, friends.
